question: In 1972, ________ coined the term ‘pyramid of numbers' that represented the total numbers of individuals (population) present in each trophic level.
solution:
The correct answer is **__Charles Elton.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **First law of thermodynamics **states that energy can neither be created nor destroyed but can be transformed from one form to another. 
 
• This represents the total number of individuals (population) present at each trophic level.
 
• The term **“pyramid of numbers”** was first coined by **Elton** in 1972.
 
• The ecological pyramids were developed by **Charles Elton**, an English zoologist, and animal ecologist, in 1927. 
 
• **They are also called Eltonian pyramids.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Eugene Pleasants Odum** was an American **biologist **at the University of Georgia known for his pioneering work on ecosystem ecology.
 
• **Ernst Heinrich Philipp **August Haeckel was a **German zoologist, naturalist, eugenicist,** philosopher, physician, professor, marine biologist, and artist.
 
• **Sir Arthur George Tansley **FLS, FRS was an English botanist and a pioneer in the science of ecology.
 
 
• **Tansle**y taught at these **universities and at Oxford,** where he served as Sherardian Professor of Botany until his retirement in 1937.
 
 
 
• Ecology was first described as a separate field of knowledge in 1866 by the German zoologist, Ernst Haeckel in his book ' Generelle Morphologie der Organismen'.
